archetype_rationale: Visa operates an interconnected payment network rather than a lending balance sheet. Its installed acceptance, issuer relationships and processing infrastructure support repeated transactions with modest physical capital requirements. That supports a compounder classification, subject to incentive competition, routing substitution, regulation and settlement losses; it does not establish acquisition returns or an unlimited runway.
framework_rationale: Retain operating_dcf for Visa's consolidated continuing parent-equity claim. The strongest alternative, financial_equity, recognizes settlement guarantees but incorrectly treats Visa as a lender: Visa does not originate cardholder credit or earn lending spreads. Existing early funding waterfalls remain. Extend the audited operating and financing projection through fiscal 2050 so the $13.137 billion principal remaining after fiscal 2031 is paid at its dated maturities. This removes the previous unsupported assumption that an interest charge alone reconciled the continuing debt claim. The owner holding period, operating normalization and independently stressed competitive duration remain separate judgments.

alternatives_considered.reason_rejected: The strongest alternative recognizes Visa's settlement guarantees, collateral and liquidity requirements. However, Visa explicitly does not issue cards, extend credit or earn the lenders' interchange economics. Bank-style distributable regulatory capital would mischaracterize its principal earnings; settlement funding is instead modeled explicitly within the operating equity claim.

Consumer payments, money movement and value-added services share infrastructure and customer relationships. The primary disclosure describes one reportable Payment Services segment and interdependent operations. Independent segment valuations would require unsupported allocations and risk counting the same network twice.

Goodwill, acquired intangibles and restricted customer funds do not measure the transferable value of the installed payment network. Asset liquidation also omits the principal source of shareholder cash.

horizon_rationale: Project every fiscal year through September 2050, the final maturity of the existing senior notes. Scheduled principal is paid from operating resources at its contractual fiscal-year maturity; interest declines with outstanding principal. No refinancing, facility renewal or owner contribution is assumed after the existing revolver expires. The seven previously declared competitive-runway years now occur explicitly in fiscal 2032–2038, followed by the declared mature growth path. Holding duration remains five years.

component_inventory.rationale: The single consolidated Payment Services claim includes consumer payments, commercial and money movement solutions, value-added services, Visa Europe and acquired processing businesses. Shared network economics are modeled once.

Settlement receivables/payables and recurring incentive funding are inside consolidated cash conversion. Restricted escrow, customer collateral and other restricted cash are excluded from opening owner cash. Client collateral mitigates guarantee losses but is not added to unrestricted parent resources.

Opening unrestricted cash, $22.586 billion senior principal and the existing committed revolver are reconciled once within the parent-equity claim. Keep the existing facility access, draw and May 2028 expiry rules. Pay $9.449 billion principal in fiscal 2027–2031 and the remaining $13.137 billion at the disclosed maturities through fiscal 2050. Fiscal 2036 includes December 2035 notes; fiscal 2046 includes December 2045 notes. Opening principal drives each year's interest budget. Final principal is paid before the continuing claim becomes debt free. No later refinancing proceeds, renewed facility, accelerated holding-date repayment or second net-debt deduction is assumed.

The disclosed available-for-sale government portfolio provides bounded emergency monetization capacity, counted only when sold and with associated income removed. Strategic equity holdings receive no separate realization proceeds; normalized margins exclude reliance on their valuation gains. Their roughly $1.2 billion carrying amount is small against annual consolidated cash generation, and no legal funding cap is inferred.

Existing acquisitions are already consolidated. BioCatch's disclosed $2.4 billion proposed cash purchase receives a $2.5 billion first-year funding budget including estimated transaction/integration cash, with no separately credited acquired earnings. Goodwill and acquired intangibles receive no additional asset value.

Normal legal costs, taxes, leases and compensation-related obligations remain within earnings and cash conversion. An additional uncovered settlement/guarantee shock is charged separately. Existing accrued litigation is not subtracted again. Escrow and conversion recoveries receive no extra cash credit; pension surplus receives no proceeds.

The verified diluted Class A-equivalent denominator assumes conversion of participating common and preferred classes against full consolidated net income. No second preferred deduction is made. The disclosed consolidation scope includes controlled entities and primary-beneficiary VIEs; the quarterly filing describes VIE investments as immaterial. No material separately attributable minority claim is identified in the supplied consolidated statements.

assumptions.rationale: Fiscal 2026 revenue rose from $40.0 billion to $45.903 billion; the June filing shows transaction growth, pricing and services contributions. Base growth decelerates as event-related marketing and pricing benefits normalize. Low represents a correlated spending, travel and routing downturn.
assumptions.counterevidence: Services growth and digital adoption could sustain faster expansion; recession and adverse routing rules could produce a deeper decline.
assumptions.falsifier: Fiscal 2027 revenue falls outside the modeled range or growth depends principally on acquisitions rather than installed-network activity.
assumptions.review_trigger: Each quarterly revenue, payments-volume and processed-transaction release.

assumptions.rationale: The second year allows partial demand recovery in the downturn and continuing digital/payment-services expansion in other cases, without restoring the low case's lost first-year revenue or margins.
assumptions.counterevidence: Travel recovery can be rapid, while regulation or lost issuer contracts can make the initial damage persistent.
assumptions.falsifier: Fiscal 2028 organic revenue contracts despite recovering payment volumes, or exceeds the high path without greater investment.
assumptions.review_trigger: Fiscal 2027 annual filing and material client-routing changes.

assumptions.rationale: Years three through five reflect nominal transaction growth, digital penetration and services sold over installed relationships. Incremental funded project earnings are added separately. Low retains a permanently smaller and less profitable franchise after the initial shock.
assumptions.counterevidence: A2A, local networks, regulatory routing and incentive competition can divert growth from Visa.
assumptions.falsifier: Processed transactions grow while net revenue persistently fails to grow, indicating declining net economics per transaction.
assumptions.review_trigger: Two quarters of divergent transaction and net-revenue trends.

assumptions.rationale: This is after-tax parent earnings before the separately modeled debt-interest charge, with SBC and normal operating expenses included. Fiscal 2026 GAAP net margin was about 51.2%; adding after-tax interest gives roughly 52.5%. Base normalization recovers only part of litigation and exceptional costs, below the full non-GAAP adjustment. Low combines weaker mix, incentives and sticky costs.
assumptions.counterevidence: Legal costs recur, wages and client marketing are rising, and higher prices may require higher incentives.
assumptions.falsifier: After-tax earnings excluding debt interest remain below 50% of revenue during normal volume growth, or adjusted margins require repeated exclusions.
assumptions.review_trigger: Annual legal-cost reconciliation and any material pricing or incentive change.

assumptions.rationale: Fiscal 2026 OCF less SBC is $22.800 billion against $23.504 billion net income, establishing conversion of approximately 0.97005 before capex. Earnings plus $1.403 billion D&A would instead be $24.907 billion: the reconciled net cash-funding deduction is $2.107 billion. The table includes a $2.040 billion litigation-accrual reduction, $612 million net incentive amortization over payments and $282 million net settlement inflow. These are distinguishable timing effects, not proof that the aggregate deduction disappears. Base retains the reported aggregate burden; low adds funding pressure and high allows limited improvement. Continuation now carries this same conversion boundary forward.
assumptions.counterevidence: Litigation payments can decline after settlements, permitting conversion recovery. Conversely, incentive renewals, taxes, receivables and settlement requirements can consume cash even when historical litigation payments reverse. Incentive and settlement inflows partly offset the reported litigation drain.
assumptions.falsifier: Across fiscal 2027-2028, OCF less SBC persistently differs from modeled conversion despite earnings being on plan; reconcile the difference to incentives, litigation, taxes and settlement balances.
assumptions.review_trigger: Each cash-flow statement, material settlement and client-incentive disclosure; assess the frozen fiscal 2027 OCF commitment.

assumptions.rationale: Base replacement spending is approximately $1.164 billion, close to $1.403 billion D&A less $229 million acquired-intangible amortization. This is an estimate, not a reported allocation. Low assumes greater replacement burden; high assumes better infrastructure utilization.
assumptions.counterevidence: Capitalized software, new security requirements and replacement costs can exceed historical depreciation.
assumptions.falsifier: Necessary replacement spending exceeds D&A for two years without corresponding capacity growth.
assumptions.review_trigger: Annual capex, software capitalization and network reliability disclosures.

assumptions.rationale: This is nominal replacement-cost escalation during the explicit expansion and competitive-fade period through fiscal 2038. Technology, security and localization spending can rise despite weak payment activity. It does not disappear at the final debt maturity: the separately declared mature_replacement_intensity establishes the fully costed renewal burden when the business enters its mature operating stage in fiscal 2039. Thereafter renewal spending scales with nominal activity, requiring procurement, architecture and productivity improvements to offset input-cost inflation. That is an uncertain operating judgment, supported by Visa's shared infrastructure and disclosed automation initiatives, rather than an automatic consequence of debt repayment.
assumptions.counterevidence: Network scaling and automation may offset input inflation sooner. Conversely, cybersecurity, resilience and data-localization obligations may prevent replacement spending from stabilizing relative to revenue; disclosed AI initiatives establish an effort, not demonstrated savings.
assumptions.falsifier: Necessary replacement spending persistently grows faster than net revenue despite mature transaction growth and completed infrastructure deployments, without offsetting productivity or pricing.
assumptions.review_trigger: Annual capex, software-capitalization, network reliability and localization disclosures; revise both the mature renewal burden and attainable growth if replacement intensity fails to stabilize.

assumptions.rationale: Separately funded platform and contract-cohort projects begin at approximately $0.309/$0.505/$0.702 billion. Base maintenance plus these projects is close to reported $1.671 billion capex. These are additional prospective projects, not addbacks of salaries, marketing or recurring incentive payments already in earnings and conversion.
assumptions.counterevidence: Disclosed capex does not identify project cohorts, and some apparent expansion may be required maintenance.
assumptions.falsifier: Capitalized project spending fails to produce measurable later services or processing earnings.
assumptions.review_trigger: Fiscal 2027 capital spending and subsequent project-cohort cash generation.

assumptions.rationale: This return applies only to separately funded platform projects in the explicit projection. Incremental after-tax project earnings equal the prior year's project investment multiplied by this assumption, with one year of deployment lag. Existing network infrastructure and distribution support high potential project returns, but expensed development and acquisition accounting obscure measured capital. These estimates do not establish the return on acquisitions, customer funding, liquidity or all continuation growth; continuation uses a separate total-parent-capital judgment.
assumptions.counterevidence: Services growth can reflect pricing or temporary marketing engagements rather than productive project investment. Incremental servicing, security and customer-acquisition costs may absorb anticipated earnings.
assumptions.falsifier: Identifiable three-year incremental after-tax project earnings divided by associated incremental parent funding remain below 20%, after recognizing deployment lags.
assumptions.review_trigger: Project deployment, subsequent cohort earnings and cash generation, and acquisition disclosures.

assumptions.rationale: The fiscal 2026 non-GAAP tax reconciliation is approximately 17.9%, while reported tax is affected by deferred benefits. Eighteen percent applies to modeled interest deductions and avoids treating the deferred benefit as recurring.
assumptions.counterevidence: Singapore incentives expire in fiscal 2028 and international tax rules can change the mix.
assumptions.falsifier: Underlying cash tax rates exceed 22% without offsetting earnings changes.
assumptions.review_trigger: Tax incentive changes, tax examinations and annual jurisdictional disclosures.

assumptions.rationale: Use a 3.4% prospective gross interest budget on each year's opening senior principal, consistent with the disclosed mix of older low-coupon notes, newer 3.8%–4.7% notes and swaps. Apply the existing tax assumption. Reserve a full year's charge in each maturity year; distribute no assumed within-year repayment saving. Principal is paid through fiscal 2050, and subsequent continuation removes the final interest charge. This is a financing budget rather than a claim that every remaining series has the same coupon.
assumptions.counterevidence: Swaps, currency movements and maturity mix make a single effective rate imperfect.
assumptions.falsifier: Annual senior interest materially exceeds opening principal times 4.2% without new borrowing.
assumptions.review_trigger: Debt issuance, swap changes and annual interest reconciliation.

assumptions.rationale: Six percent is a prospective cash-cost budget for contingent floating-rate borrowing, including the facility's rating-dependent margin. It is not asserted to be the current reference rate. The structural borrowing test uses a higher cost.
assumptions.counterevidence: Actual reference rates and credit spreads can be substantially lower or higher.
assumptions.falsifier: A required draw can only be funded outside the modeled cost bounds.
assumptions.review_trigger: Facility draw, rating change or refinancing disclosure.

assumptions.rationale: Projected committed capacity is limited to the disclosed undrawn $7 billion facility, with Schedule 1 commitments totaling that amount. It is available through May 2028 only; no extension or replacement facility is assumed.
assumptions.counterevidence: Commitments can terminate following default, and lender nonperformance can reduce effective capacity.
assumptions.falsifier: An amendment, termination or reduction lowers committed capacity before expiry.
assumptions.review_trigger: Any facility amendment, default notice or lender failure.

assumptions.rationale: Current covenant compliance and no outstanding facility borrowing support access in the ordinary cases. Section 4.3 requires no Default and accurate applicable representations plus a borrowing notice; Sections 5.5 and 5.7 are excepted after closing, so an earnings decline alone is not treated as an automatic MAC draw prohibition. Zero access is explicitly executed in stress tests.
assumptions.counterevidence: Default, inaccurate representations, operational delay or lender failure can prevent timely funding.
assumptions.falsifier: A compliant borrowing request is rejected or required funding arrives after the payment deadline.
assumptions.review_trigger: Any settlement event, covenant issue or borrowing request.

assumptions.rationale: A draw outstanding from the first-year event is repaid at May 2028 expiry, approximately eight months into fiscal 2028. No automatic rollover is embedded.
assumptions.counterevidence: Earlier voluntary repayment would reduce cost; an amendment could change timing.
assumptions.falsifier: A binding amendment changes the termination date.
assumptions.review_trigger: Facility amendment or repayment.

assumptions.rationale: Management held $9.9 billion of total available liquidity for daily settlement contingencies. This is the operating-liquidity anchor, inclusive of undrawn commitments rather than an additional cash deduction. Required cash rises as the facility is drawn or expires.
assumptions.counterevidence: Brazil guarantee expansion, concentration or collateral deterioration could require a larger buffer.
assumptions.falsifier: Disclosed settlement requirements or losses demonstrate that $15 billion is insufficient under comparable activity.
assumptions.review_trigger: Settlement exposure, collateral, Brazil rules or concentrated client distress.

assumptions.rationale: Use the declared liquidity-buffer growth rates through fiscal 2031. Subsequently grow the operating buffer with positive nominal revenue growth; declining activity releases no buffer automatically. This ties later collateral and settlement capacity to the explicitly fading activity path rather than compounding an early expansion rate through 2050. Stress higher initial buffer needs together with weaker operating conversion and capital returns.
assumptions.counterevidence: Netting and collateral improvements can reduce liquidity needs; guarantee expansion can increase them faster.
assumptions.falsifier: Required liquidity grows materially faster than nominal activity for two reporting periods.
assumptions.review_trigger: Annual peak settlement exposure and collateral disclosures.

assumptions.rationale: Subtracting reported SBC from OCF funds a cash-equivalent compensation policy with constant diluted shares. The baseline factor of one adds no second charge. A structural test increases cash needed above reported fair-value compensation, rather than granting free share shrinkage.
assumptions.counterevidence: Actual award settlement and dilution offset can cost more than accounting SBC.
assumptions.falsifier: Compensation-related cash funding persistently exceeds twice reported SBC or diluted shares rise despite the funding reserve.
assumptions.review_trigger: Annual grants, diluted-share reconciliation and employee-plan cash flows.

assumptions.rationale: The first-year funding estimate covers the disclosed $2.4 billion BioCatch cash consideration plus estimated execution and integration cash. It is a forecast budget, not a legal liability cap. No acquired earnings or sale proceeds are credited; larger obligations require revision.
assumptions.counterevidence: Closing is conditional, consideration adjustments and assumed obligations may differ, and useful acquired earnings could emerge.
assumptions.falsifier: Binding transaction disclosures establish total parent cash needs above $2.8 billion or materially different consideration scope.
assumptions.review_trigger: Closing announcement, purchase-price allocation and acquired-obligation disclosures.

assumptions.rationale: The low case includes an additional $3 billion uncovered settlement/guarantee loss beyond normal charges. Structural tests examine much larger failures against disclosed maximum daily exposure of $168.6 billion and collateral of $9.7 billion. This is a net parent funding judgment, not an estimate of gross legal damages or a liability cap.
assumptions.counterevidence: Historical guarantee losses are minimal and responsibility plans mitigate covered litigation; correlated failures and uncovered legal claims could be much larger.
assumptions.falsifier: New net obligations or client concentration invalidate the selected stress scale.
assumptions.review_trigger: Client default, guarantee expansion, adverse judgment or responsibility-plan impairment.

assumptions.rationale: The funding test places payment at the end of the first future fiscal quarter. Only that quarter's generated cash, net of investment and compensation funding, is available before the deadline; later-year cash cannot rescue the payment.
assumptions.counterevidence: Actual settlement events can occur sooner and with less warning.
assumptions.falsifier: A material obligation becomes payable before the modeled quarter-end funding window.
assumptions.review_trigger: Any material settlement or acceleration deadline.

assumptions.rationale: Emergency proceeds are bounded by the disclosed $850 million available-for-sale government-debt portfolio. Only the required amount is monetized, once, before borrowing. Strategic private equities, escrow and customer collateral are not assumed immediately available.
assumptions.counterevidence: Market disruption, operational timing or portfolio changes may impair realizability.
assumptions.falsifier: The unrestricted government portfolio falls below the budget or cannot settle before the funding deadline.
assumptions.review_trigger: Investment maturity/restriction disclosures or a funding event.

assumptions.rationale: Two percent is an after-tax prospective earnings budget removed when emergency government investments are sold. It prevents monetizing the asset while retaining its income in normalized margins.
assumptions.counterevidence: Actual portfolio yields and tax treatment may differ.
assumptions.falsifier: Disclosed recurring portfolio income falls outside the assumed yield bounds.
assumptions.review_trigger: Portfolio sale or annual investment-income disclosure.

assumptions.rationale: A 9.5% nominal USD owner hurdle reflects a cash-generative global network with limited ordinary borrowing needs but material regulatory, competition and settlement-tail exposure. It is an explicit required-return judgment, not a market-derived fact. Operating downside and executed insolvency are modeled in cash flows, so the hurdle is held constant across cases.
assumptions.counterevidence: Network durability may warrant a lower hurdle; legal and routing disruption may warrant a higher one.
assumptions.falsifier: A persistent change in business concentration, settlement exposure or financing access changes the claim's risk.
assumptions.review_trigger: Material regulation, client concentration, leverage or guarantee changes.

assumptions.rationale: Apply the previously declared first three continuation-year growth judgments explicitly in fiscal 2032–2034. Digital adoption, issuer integration and services support persistence; alternative rails, routing and client bargaining support low-case erosion. These years are economic runway, independent of both the five-year holding period and the debt projection's length.
assumptions.counterevidence: Distribution advantages may persist much longer, or routing displacement may accelerate.
assumptions.falsifier: Transaction retention and net revenue per transaction indicate materially faster erosion or stronger persistence than forecast.
assumptions.review_trigger: Annual competitive, routing and customer-incentive disclosures.

assumptions.rationale: Apply four further competitive-fade years explicitly in fiscal 2035–2038. Lower growth reflects competing rails, incentive bargaining and maturation. Later fiscal years use terminal_growth. Structural tests now vary these explicit growth assumptions because the contractual debt projection extends beyond the competitive runway.
assumptions.counterevidence: New payment use cases may prolong growth; regulation can compress economics sooner.
assumptions.falsifier: Mature-market net economics fail to exhibit the expected competitive fade.
assumptions.review_trigger: Annual mature-market growth, pricing and routing outcomes.

assumptions.rationale: Mature nominal growth is modest relative to recent transaction and services expansion. Low assumes no eventual growth after permanent revenue and margin damage. Positive growth requires investment at the declared incremental parent-equity return; no inventory or working-capital liquidation funds it.
assumptions.counterevidence: Cash displacement may sustain stronger growth, while fee regulation or alternative rails may cause lasting contraction.
assumptions.falsifier: Mature-market nominal owner earnings persistently contract or require more investment than the declared return permits.
assumptions.review_trigger: Annual mature-market earnings, customer funding and competitive supply evidence.

assumptions.rationale: Re-underwrite these bounds as incremental recurring after-tax parent cash earnings divided by incremental NONLIQUID operating equity, excluding the operating-liquidity buffer retained separately in each explicit bridge. The ID is preserved, but its previously inconsistent scope is corrected. The denominator includes additional platform, receivable and customer-contract capital beyond recurring funding already deducted in cash conversion; it excludes acquisitions without modeled acquired earnings. Visa's shared processing infrastructure and installed customer distribution support returns above the financing hurdle, while client-incentive assets, receivables, security spending and expensed development argue against using the narrower platform-project return of 20%/40%/60%. The broader operating bounds remain 12%/22%/32% after reconsideration; they are deployment estimates, not observed cohort returns. Explicit total deployment equals operating growth investment plus separately retained liquidity. Continuation derives a LOWER blended return by adding required incremental liquidity to the operating-capital denominator, rather than applying this operating return to total capital.
assumptions.counterevidence: Installed-network pricing and transaction growth may need less additional operating capital than assumed. Conversely, incentive competition, poor acquired-platform integration and security obligations may depress incremental cash returns. Reported asset changes contain acquisitions, amortization and currency effects and cannot establish organic cohort returns directly.
assumptions.falsifier: Over three reporting years, identifiable incremental recurring parent cash earnings divided by lagged incremental nonliquid operating equity persistently falls below 12% or exceeds 32%, after separating recurring cash funding, acquisitions and retained settlement liquidity.
assumptions.review_trigger: Annual incentive-asset, receivable and capital-spending reconciliations; project-cohort cash outcomes; settlement-liquidity requirements. Re-estimate operating and liquid capital separately.

assumptions.rationale: Preserve the existing numerical year-five cash normalization: terminal_owner_earnings plus maintenance_5 and extra_sbc_5 equals generation_5 when this multiplier is one. Divide that sum by generation_5, using a positive denominator only in the already liquidated state, and multiply conversion by the resulting ratio for fiscal 2032 onward. Thus base continuation retains the reported cash-conversion burden, while higher reserve multipliers reduce subsequent cash generation before growth investment. No litigation or customer-funding recovery appears automatically at realization.
assumptions.counterevidence: The $2.040 billion litigation-accrual drain can reverse, and some collection movements may normalize. However, the same cash-flow table contains $894 million combined incentive and settlement inflows; reversing only adverse items would overstate normalization. Continuing legal provisions and customer funding argue against assuming complete recovery.
assumptions.falsifier: A two-year cash-flow reconciliation demonstrates a durable reduction or increase in the net operating cash reserve after excluding asset sales, acquisition effects and settlement-balance liquidation.
assumptions.review_trigger: Annual reconciliation of OCF less SBC to earnings and D&A, including litigation, incentives, taxes and settlement movements.

assumptions.rationale: Forecast fiscal 2033 principal using Note 10's $700 million February 2033 dollar notes plus $1.133 billion May 2033 euro notes translated at the frozen reporting-date exchange rate. This is a future USD payment convention, not a new current-balance observation.
assumptions.counterevidence: Euro exchange rates and hedge settlements can change the eventual USD payment.
assumptions.falsifier: A debt amendment, redemption or currency reconciliation changes the dated principal obligation or its USD funding need.
assumptions.review_trigger: Every annual debt table, redemption notice and material exchange-rate or swap change.

assumptions.rationale: Forecast the June 2034 euro-note maturity at Note 10's frozen September 2026 translation of $737 million. Keep the same currency convention as opening principal.
assumptions.counterevidence: Future exchange rates and hedge cash settlements can differ from the frozen translation.
assumptions.falsifier: Updated contractual principal or currency terms change this payment.
assumptions.review_trigger: Annual debt and derivatives disclosures.

assumptions.rationale: Fiscal 2036 includes the $1.5 billion dollar notes due December 2035 and $650 million dollar notes due February 2036. Calendar December 2035 belongs to the fiscal year ending September 2036.
assumptions.counterevidence: Permitted redemptions or amendments could change payment timing or add redemption costs.
assumptions.falsifier: A binding debt transaction changes these principal amounts or dates.
assumptions.review_trigger: Debt amendments, tenders, redemptions and annual maturity tables.

assumptions.rationale: Forecast the May 2037 euro-note maturity at the $737 million frozen reporting-date translation in Note 10.
assumptions.counterevidence: Exchange rates and hedge settlements can change the actual USD funding requirement.
assumptions.falsifier: Updated principal or currency terms differ from this frozen projection.
assumptions.review_trigger: Annual debt, currency and derivatives disclosures.

assumptions.rationale: Forecast payment of the disclosed $1 billion dollar notes due April 2040 at their contractual maturity.
assumptions.counterevidence: Redemption or amendment could alter timing and transaction costs.
assumptions.falsifier: A binding debt transaction changes the obligation.
assumptions.review_trigger: Debt transactions and annual maturity tables.

assumptions.rationale: Forecast the May 2044 euro-note maturity using Note 10's $680 million reporting-date translation, consistently with opening debt.
assumptions.counterevidence: Exchange rates and hedges can change eventual USD cash requirements.
assumptions.falsifier: Updated contractual or currency terms invalidate the frozen payment convention.
assumptions.review_trigger: Annual debt and derivatives disclosures.

assumptions.rationale: The $3.5 billion dollar notes due December 2045 are paid in fiscal 2046, not fiscal 2045. Preserve their disclosed calendar maturity within the annual fiscal bridge.
assumptions.counterevidence: A future redemption or amendment can alter timing or costs.
assumptions.falsifier: A binding debt transaction changes this principal payment.
assumptions.review_trigger: Debt transactions and annual maturity tables.

assumptions.rationale: Forecast the disclosed $750 million dollar-note payment in September 2047. The final fiscal 2050 payment is the remaining principal balance, which reconciles to the disclosed $1.75 billion August 2050 notes.
assumptions.counterevidence: Future debt transactions can change the maturity profile.
assumptions.falsifier: Updated debt terms change either obligation or the remaining-principal reconciliation.
assumptions.review_trigger: Annual debt tables and debt transactions.

assumptions.rationale: At the independently modeled mature operating stage in fiscal 2039, increase the preceding year's replacement budget, scaled for mature revenue growth, by 50%/20%/5%. Thereafter hold this higher renewal intensity relative to nominal revenue. The base uplift is anchored to fiscal 2026 total property, equipment and technology purchases of $1.671 billion versus $1.403 billion D&A, a ratio near 1.19; using this relationship for mature replacement is a judgment because current purchases include expansion and D&A includes acquired intangibles. The low uplift reserves substantially more for persistent security, resilience and localization requirements; the high uplift requires stronger infrastructure utilization and automation. Visa's integrated global network and disclosed internal AI efficiencies support testing a stable mature spending ratio, while rising network and personnel expenses contradict assuming effortless productivity. The transition begins with operating maturity, twelve years before the projection ends, and has no connection to the final note maturity. The uplift is maintenance, earns no incremental growth credit, and remains embedded in terminal earnings.
assumptions.counterevidence: Neither filing demonstrates that renewal costs will stabilize relative to revenue in 2039. Security threats, country-specific infrastructure, software obsolescence and weak pricing could require continuing increases. AI adoption may add costs before producing efficiencies.
assumptions.falsifier: During normal transaction growth, necessary replacement spending and reliability obligations consume a persistently rising share of revenue after excluding identifiable capacity expansion; productivity and pricing fail to offset the increase.
assumptions.review_trigger: Review each annual capital-spending and network-cost disclosure. Raise the mature intensity, reduce achievable margins or rebuild the continuing-business hypothesis if replacement intensity fails to stabilize; do not postpone the transition merely to the last projected debt payment.

normalization.conclusion: Fiscal 2026 revenue, net income and OCF are $45.903/$23.504/$23.728 billion. Base preinterest after-tax margin of 55% recovers only part of exceptional legal and other costs; the low case cuts revenue 15% and margin to 45%, preserving permanent damage rather than applying a cheaper multiple to peak earnings.

working_capital.conclusion: Fiscal 2026 OCF less SBC is $22.800 billion, $704 million below net income. Earnings plus D&A is $24.907 billion, so the complete net operating cash reserve is $2.107 billion. The cash-flow table separately identifies a $2.040 billion litigation-accrual drain, $612 million incentive amortization over cash payments and $282 million net settlement inflow; the remaining movements net to a $961 million drain. These figures reconcile to $2.107 billion. Neither the favorable movements nor reversal of the adverse litigation movement is extrapolated independently. Explicit conversion retains the aggregate burden, and the revised terminal graph carries it forward. Additional continuation capital covers incremental requirements beyond recurring cash funding already charged.

maintenance_and_growth_capex.conclusion: Fiscal 2026 property, equipment and technology purchases of $1.671 billion and D&A of $1.403 billion anchor spending judgments, without proving a maintenance allocation. The first five years retain separate maintenance and funded platform projects with lagged earnings. Broader operating growth investment thereafter excludes separately retained settlement liquidity from its return denominator. Replacement-cost escalation continues through fiscal 2038. At operating maturity in fiscal 2039, maintenance receives a 50%/20%/5% intensity uplift and then scales with nominal revenue; this explicitly requires productivity and pricing to offset input inflation. The higher maintenance level carries into terminal owner earnings. A structural alternative combines twelve years of 8% replacement escalation with a threefold mature renewal burden, weaker margins and cash conversion. Recurring salaries, incentives and SBC remain charged once; acquisition spending is not relabeled maintenance.

financing_scope.conclusion: Use $12.938 billion unrestricted opening cash, excluding escrow and customer funds. The existing $7 billion committed facility retains its access conditions, draw accounting and May 2028 repayment/expiry. Extend every annual bridge through fiscal 2050: $22.586 billion opening senior principal less $9.449 billion fiscal 2027–2031 payments leaves $13.137 billion; subsequent dated payments exhaust that balance. Interest follows opening principal. No refinancing or owner funding is assumed after facility expiry. Early denied-access alternatives still execute liquidation and preserve unpaid creditor principal. A separate persistent cash squeeze tests the entire maturity schedule with no refinancing.

dilution.conclusion: Use current verified fiscal 2026 diluted shares of 1.907 billion Class A equivalents. Note 16 includes assumed conversion of participating common and preferred securities, with the diluted numerator equal to consolidated net income. Replace all prior share-observation bindings with obs_1e2a0ad9a267756f31cc. Future shares remain constant under cash-equivalent compensation and pro-rata distributions: subtract reported SBC from OCF and separately stress excess funding. No free buyback shrinkage or second preferred claim is modeled. V is ordinary Class A common stock and listing_ratio is null; no ADR conversion applies.

terminal.conclusion: The sole continuation begins after fiscal 2050, but mature operating economics begin in fiscal 2039. Revenue and replacement spending share mature nominal growth throughout fiscal 2039–2050 after a separately charged renewal-intensity uplift; no replacement-cost erosion vanishes at the last debt maturity. Continuing productivity is an explicit uncertain operating hypothesis, challenged by permanently higher maintenance intensity. Terminal earnings retain reconciled cash conversion, maintenance and compensation costs. Explicit growth returns exclude separately retained liquidity; terminal blended return adds liquidity capital algebraically, so future operating investment and buffer growth are both funded exactly once. Scheduled debt remains paid through 2050, with interest released only after repayment. Retained liquidity receives no separate sale proceeds.

method_selection.conclusion: A levered operating DCF captures the single network's economic claim. Visa's settlement guarantees require a funding waterfall, but its explicit nonlender business model rejects bank-capital valuation. Acquired intangibles and network effects also reject asset NAV as the principal framework.

scenario_coherence.conclusion: Demand, margins, recurring cash funding, competition and settlement losses retain their correlated scenario paths and executed denied-credit failures. The revised operating-return denominator excludes liquidity retained separately in explicit years; continuation adds that capital through its derived blended return. Mature maintenance assumptions preserve a substantially heavier renewal burden in the low case and require demonstrated productivity rather than relying on the final debt date. The added persistent-cost-pressure alternative combines prolonged input-cost escalation, permanently higher replacement intensity, weak monetization and cash conversion, lower operating returns and unavailable credit. The existing full-maturity squeeze and longer-persistence alternatives remain; no favorable probability weights are asserted.

components.claim_scope: The continuing consolidated parent-equity claim per diluted Class A-equivalent ordinary share, including all participating classes on an as-converted basis.
components.scope_reconciliation: The component remains consolidated parent equity per verified diluted Class A-equivalent ordinary share. Recurring customer funding, normal legal expenses, taxes and reported SBC remain embedded in earnings or reconciled cash conversion. Explicit fiscal 2032–2050 growth investment uses incremental NONLIQUID operating-equity returns; increases in required settlement liquidity are separately retained, so these uses no longer overlap in the stated capital denominator. Terminal continuation derives a blended return that includes both operating investment and incremental liquidity, with no separate second liquidity charge. Maintenance escalates with replacement costs through fiscal 2038, receives a separately declared mature renewal-intensity uplift in fiscal 2039, and thereafter scales with nominal activity. This operating transition is independent of the final debt maturity. All dated principal payments, interest changes, facility expiry and existing failure rules remain intact. Restricted escrow and customer collateral remain excluded from usable owner cash; acquisitions receive their stated funding budgets without invented earnings. Constant shares require cash-equivalent compensation funding and pro-rata distributions, without free buyback shrinkage.

terminal.rationale: The seven exceptional-growth fade years remain explicit in fiscal 2032–2038. Mature replacement economics begin explicitly in fiscal 2039: maintenance receives the declared intensity uplift and subsequently scales with nominal revenue. Thus maintenance and revenue already share the mature growth basis for twelve audited years before continuation; final debt repayment does not change replacement economics. final_owner_earnings deducts this fully costed maintenance, continuing cash-conversion burdens and excess compensation funding, and removes senior interest only after final principal payment. It is before growth investment. The operating-return assumption now excludes separately retained settlement liquidity. Continuation restores the total-parent-capital boundary algebraically: inverse blended return equals inverse operating return plus required closing liquidity divided by mature owner earnings. For positive growth, the compiler therefore charges owner earnings times growth divided by operating return PLUS required liquidity times growth, exactly once. Negative growth releases neither operating capital nor liquidity automatically. The failure-state denominator safeguard uses existing cont_dummy only after liquidation; failed common ownership retains zero earnings and proceeds. No retained-cash sale, duplicate net-debt deduction or manual realization is added.

earning_power.assessment: Installed transaction growth and net monetization drive earnings, while net margin includes operating costs, taxes and SBC before separately charged debt interest. Fiscal 2026 earnings are not treated as a riskless peak: the low path loses revenue, margin and cash conversion together. Base normalization excludes reliance on equity-investment gains and restores only part of exceptional costs.

reinvestment.assessment: Separate existing earning power, narrow funded platform projects, broader incremental operating capital and settlement liquidity. The preserved return ID now expressly measures incremental recurring parent cash earnings divided by incremental nonliquid operating equity. Customer-contract and receivable expansion beyond recurring cash funding belong in that denominator; separately retained liquidity does not. Explicit payouts deduct operating investment and liquidity retention once each. Continuation uses a derived blended return whose inverse adds operating capital per dollar of incremental earnings and required liquidity per dollar of mature earnings. This reproduces both funding uses without overlap. Maintenance receives an explicit mature renewal uplift before continuation and earns no project-return credit. Historical accounting ROIC establishes neither these deployment returns nor acquisition payback.

competitive_response.assessment: Competing networks, local rails, A2A and issuer bargaining constrain net monetization. Retain the original installed-growth scenarios through 2031, then project the seven declared competitive-fade years explicitly in 2032–2038. Faster erosion and longer persistence now change those explicit growth assumptions rather than scaling an empty terminal runway. Fiscal 2039 onward is mature growth; the long debt projection grants no extra moat duration.

customer_value.assessment: Authorization, fraud reduction, acceptance, reconciliation and processing reliability provide customer value. Issuers and acquirers retain the direct customer relationships and can bargain over incentives or routing. Pricing is therefore constrained by retention and service value; the low case combines lower net revenue and margin rather than assuming price increases are costless.

capital_allocation.assessment: Constant ordinary-equivalent shares and cash-equivalent pro-rata payouts remain the allocation convention. Reported SBC and stressed excess compensation funding prevent free dilution offsets. Annual cash pays maintenance, operating growth investment, acquisitions where declared, scheduled principal and separately retained settlement liquidity before distributions. The operating-return denominator excludes that retained liquidity; terminal reinvestment uses the derived total-capital return instead. Mature replacement spending includes the additional renewal-intensity burden, reducing distributable cash without creating growth earnings. The existing facility expires in 2028 and no later refinancing or owner contributions are assumed. Retained buffer cash and financial assets receive no duplicate realization.

financing_survival.assessment: The early deadline waterfall remains unchanged. Later survival no longer depends on an unspecified rollover: the existing revolver expires in 2028, and every senior maturity through 2050 is paid from annual operating resources with lower common payouts. Opening debt controls interest, and unpaid early-failure debt is preserved outside the liquidated common operating claim. The persistent maturity squeeze directly tests operating weakness with no subsequent credit. No long-dated principal is repaid merely at the holding date.

inflation.assessment: All forecasts remain nominal USD. Revenue growth already includes pricing and currency judgments, while early maintenance follows replacement-cost escalation independently. Persistent adverse input inflation cannot be silently removed at debt maturity. Instead, fiscal 2039 marks the previously modeled mature operating stage: a separately declared renewal-intensity uplift funds a higher maintenance base, after which productivity, procurement and architecture must offset input inflation sufficiently to stabilize maintenance relative to nominal revenue. Shared processing infrastructure and disclosed automation initiatives support this hypothesis; increasing security, personnel and localization costs challenge it. The cost-pressure alternative compounds 8% replacement escalation through fiscal 2038 and triples the mature replacement base, retaining that adverse intensity indefinitely. This tests prolonged cost growth and permanent margin damage; it does not assert that costs can grow faster than revenue forever while the same going concern remains viable.

realization.assessment: The five-year owner holding period and projection through the final fiscal 2050 note maturity remain separate. Trusted code values all remaining shareholder distributions and one continuing claim at the holding date. Mature replacement economics now begin explicitly in fiscal 2039 and persist through realization, so the last principal payment changes financing costs alone. The terminal blended return funds both nonliquid growth capital and growing operating liquidity, consistent with the explicit payout boundary. No retained-cash realization, second exit or blanket net-debt deduction is supplied. Existing early insolvency still extinguishes every subsequent common payout and terminal earning while preserving unpaid senior claims.

hypotheses.explanation: Acceptance, issuer integration and processing reliability allow transactions and services to grow without proportional replacement capital. Pricing persists when it improves approval, fraud and reconciliation outcomes.
hypotheses.counterevidence: Issuers own customer relationships; local rails and A2A can bypass network processing, while pricing can provoke routing and incentive concessions.
hypotheses.discriminating_observation: Over the next two fiscal years, processed-transaction growth accompanied by stable net revenue per transaction and stable cash conversion would support persistence; volume growth with deteriorating net economics would reject it.

hypotheses.explanation: Recent growth partly reflects pricing and event-related services demand. Competitive networks and customers capture a rising share through incentives and alternative routing, reducing margin and the competitive runway.
hypotheses.counterevidence: Broad digital adoption, tokenization and the scale of Visa's acceptance network can sustain customer value despite competition.
hypotheses.discriminating_observation: Compare annual incentive cash payments and net revenue growth with processed transactions, client retention and mature-market routing share; worsening net economics despite healthy payment demand supports erosion.

hypotheses.explanation: Higher platform spending and acquisitions may create later earnings, but services revenue growth alone does not prove a return on the purchase price or new capital. The model credits only separately funded organic projects after a lag and no BioCatch earnings.
hypotheses.counterevidence: Prisma/Newpay and fraud tools can strengthen network relationships and produce synergies not separately disclosed.
hypotheses.discriminating_observation: Track identifiable incremental after-tax earnings and subsequent cash generation against cumulative parent project and acquisition funding over three years; repeated spending without later cash refutes an investment-phase explanation.

hypotheses.explanation: Ordinary cash generation, eligible government investments and a compliant committed draw can bridge a moderate client loss. Correlated defaults, uncovered claims or unavailable credit can instead consume all common equity before later operating cash arrives.
hypotheses.counterevidence: Historical guarantee losses have been minimal and collateral and responsibility plans mitigate exposure.
hypotheses.discriminating_observation: A real stress event should reveal net losses, collateral realization, notice-to-funding time and facility availability; timely borrowing with maintained liquidity supports fundability, while missed senior payment rejects it.

hypotheses.explanation: Fiscal 2026 conversion weakness may primarily reflect litigation-payment timing, or recurring customer, tax and collection needs may absorb the eventual litigation recovery. The model preserves the aggregate cash reserve rather than capitalizing an unobserved recovery.
hypotheses.counterevidence: The $2.040 billion litigation-accrual drain is identifiable and could diminish substantially. Conversely, reported incentive and settlement inflows temporarily supported cash, while client guarantees and incentive assets expanded.
hypotheses.discriminating_observation: For fiscal 2027 and 2028, reconcile OCF less SBC against net income and D&A, separately measuring litigation accrual changes, incentive amortization versus payments, taxes and net settlement movements. Durable conversion recovery after removing settlement releases supports timing reversal; offsetting customer and tax demands support persistent funding.

hypotheses.explanation: Visa's recurring network cash can pay existing senior principal at its dated maturities while preserving operating liquidity, permitting a continuing claim without assuming refinancing. The competing explanation is that incentive funding, lower monetization and replacement costs absorb the cash, forcing payout reductions or new financing.
hypotheses.counterevidence: Recent repurchases and dividends exceeded operating cash after investment, and management retains borrowing access. Future acquisitions, guarantee requirements or uncovered claims can consume the modeled debt-service capacity.
hypotheses.discriminating_observation: For each future fiscal year compare operating cash less maintenance, compensation funding and actual acquisitions with scheduled principal and required liquidity retention. Repeated borrowing to fund those uses despite reduced common payouts would reject the modeled self-funding path.

hypotheses.explanation: Visa's shared network, installed acceptance and automation may let mature replacement spending stabilize relative to nominal revenue after funding a higher renewal burden. The competing explanation is that cybersecurity, localization and software obsolescence force replacement intensity to keep rising, exhausting pricing and productivity gains. The model adopts stabilization from fiscal 2039, independent of debt maturity, and charges an explicit uplift before that assumption takes effect.
hypotheses.counterevidence: The filings describe automation initiatives but do not demonstrate the required sustained productivity. Network, personnel and capital spending are increasing, and regulatory fragmentation can duplicate infrastructure.
hypotheses.discriminating_observation: Reconcile annual property, equipment and technology purchases, D&A, processing volumes, network costs and reliability outcomes. A persistently rising necessary replacement share of net revenue despite normal volume growth rejects stabilization and requires a new mature cash-flow path.

forecast_commitments.scope: Visa Inc. consolidated senior notes; principal only, excluding commercial paper, interest and issuance costs

structural_tests.rationale: A spending/routing downturn can coincide with client distress, weaker conversion and denied credit. The $30 billion net payment exceeds predeadline resources and executes common insolvency rather than substituting a higher discount rate.

A $12 billion first-quarter loss during a moderate operating downturn requires actual portfolio monetization and a committed draw. Draw cost, reduced undrawn liquidity and May 2028 repayment are included, so a borrowed dollar is not also counted as undrawn capacity.

A larger first-quarter obligation with unavailable facility access cannot be financed from later operating cash. The waterfall pays available senior resources, retains unpaid debt claims and sets all later common distributions and continuation earnings to zero.

Alternative rails and issuer bargaining can reduce installed growth, margins, deployment returns and persistence together. The competitive period is now explicit, so execute erosion directly in those annual growth drivers rather than scaling an empty post-2050 runway.

Embedded issuer infrastructure, acceptance and new use cases may preserve superior growth through more of the explicit 2032–2038 period. Increase the later-stage growth path while retaining the same five-year holding period, required return, dated principal payments and mature economics.

Client bargaining and expanded guarantees jointly weaken recurring cash conversion, increase the continuing cash-funding reserve and require more nonliquid operating capital per dollar of incremental earnings. The 8% override now applies solely to nonliquid operating equity; explicit liquidity retention remains additional and terminal continuation adds it through the blended return. Lower achievable growth accompanies weaker returns. All dated debt payments and higher initial liquidity requirements remain funded within the executed projection.

Test the full existing maturity schedule with an initial demand contraction, permanently weaker monetization and conversion, declining installed activity, higher replacement costs and excess compensation funding. Subsequent nominal growth stops, common payouts absorb debt service, and no facility or refinancing proceeds rescue the claim. This tests sustained self-funding rather than merely the original first-quarter failure event.

Test the productivity hypothesis against prolonged adverse input-cost growth and permanent renewal-intensity damage. Replacement costs compound at 8% through fiscal 2038, then the mature replacement budget is tripled and remains elevated relative to revenue indefinitely. Weaker demand, monetization and recurring cash conversion coincide with lower operating investment returns and unavailable facility access. Mature growth is zero, preventing favorable growth assumptions from masking the cash cost. This is a structural test of a much heavier enduring maintenance franchise, separate from a discount-rate change or the last debt maturity.

failure_states.rationale: Only opening unrestricted cash, first-quarter cash generation net of contemporaneous investment and excess compensation, eligible government-portfolio proceeds and timely accessible borrowing fund the payment deadline. Restricted customer funds, later operating cash and owner contributions are unavailable. If the deadline obligation cannot be funded, the business enters the modeled liquidation state and all outstanding note and drawn-facility principal becomes a senior liquidation claim. This is a failure-state liquidation assumption, not automatic acceleration merely because revenue declines. Senior_paid=min(resources,senior_due), unpaid=senior_due-senior_paid and equity_residual=resources-senior_paid. The principal-allocation subgraph preserves unpaid principal, and senior payments enter annual other claims once. Failure leaves zero closing resources after paying available senior claims, stops later operations and common payouts, and removes future operating buffer requirements through survival. It neither injects cash nor cancels creditor claims. Surviving firms retain the full operating-liquidity requirement, including repayment and expiry of committed borrowing.
failure_states.payment_timing: End of fiscal 2027 first quarter, before any common distribution; eligible borrowing and government-security proceeds must settle before this deadline.

holding_horizon_rationale: Retain the independently selected five-year owner evaluation period. It permits assessment of client retention, services economics and acquisition integration. The longer audited projection exists to discharge dated creditor obligations, not to extend the holding period or improve the reported return. Trusted code must value all later shareholder cash and the single continuation realization at year five.
